definitions: Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish geographer, cosmographer and cartographer. He is most renowned for creating the Mercator projection, a new type of map projection based on mathematical calculations.

The Mercator projection is a cylindrical map projection presented by Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It became the standard map projection for nautical charts because of its ability to represent lines of constant course as straight lines.
examples: The Mercator projection distorts land masses near the poles.
Many atlases still use a form of the Mercator projection.
